headline: The clap test now only trusts the button it tells you to press
lede: An audit found the ±50 ms audio-alignment proof could be fooled: a lagging phone mic could borrow a nearby steering flick as its 'tap' and grade green. Claps now pair only with A-button presses — the one control the instructions name — and a new harness mutant proves the old attack stays dead. Phone-take coverage deepened too: Android webm files now travel the whole store-to-verify pipeline, and a dropped audio tail finally has a name.

notes.text: Clap grading is A-button-only (SHAPE-fail-closed): steering/analog edges are reported as context but can never absorb a clap; dense-stick + 120 ms-shifted-tap mutant ships red-proof in recordcheck (123/123).

#2093: webm phone takes verify end-to-end in the evidence self-test (35/35), the clap verdict prints container duration with a tail-drop warning, and voiceFlushTimedOut names the flush-timeout outcome instead of shipping voiceless in silence.

Filed #2136: the synth clap ±50 gate is box-load-flaky — and was already flaky on main before this change (press-arrival jitter under CDP; the audio side is rock-stable). Needs an answer before the clap line can certify on a busy machine.
#1711 stays open with next: the three fresh phone takes (one clapping) are Jon's line to cross; the relabel tool is the lane-doable piece left on #2093.
